text:
nina: FYI hitting a nasty dup-post/retry loop in sampleapp when running in a background service on Android 13. after a connect timeout the SDK retries and triggers an auth refresh; the refresh itself retries a POST and we end up with two identical requests. anyone seen retry+auth race on mobile?
rafael: ouch. is the retry happening in OkHttp or in our SDK layer?
nina: looks like SDK-level retry for idempotent heuristics kicks in, and our token refresh interceptor calls the same API to exchange a refresh token (POST). the SDK sees the POST as safe to retry after connect timeout and replays it while the interceptor is still performing refresh.
chloe: can you paste the interceptor ordering? if auth interceptor runs after retry interceptor or vice-versa that matters.
nina: snippet from client setup:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor(maxRetries = 2))
  .callTimeout(45, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```
nina: AuthInterceptor does synchronous refresh on 401 by blocking and doing a blocking POST. but when connect times out we get a retry and the refresh POST can be duplicated.
sam: hmm two issues: 1) blocking refresh on main/dispatcher and 2) RetryInterceptor treats refresh POST as safe. Solutions: mark token-exchange endpoints as non-retriable, and make refresh async or use call.clone() carefully.
rafael: also Android 13 network stack changed some timeouts so the connect may fail faster, increasing window for races. We should make the refresh call use a separate client with retries disabled.
nina: tried that locally: creating a clientNoRetry for refresh endpoint fixed duplicates. but sampleapp still had occasional stalls when cancelling the refresh call from a service shutdown.
chloe: service shutdown cancelling is another angle. Are you cancelling coroutines without cancelling underlying calls? that can leave in-flight calls retrying.
nina: yes cancelling service job cancels coroutine but our refresh call used synchronous execute(), not cancellable. changing to enqueue + callback or suspend await with invokeOnCancellation fixed clean shuts.
sam: propose SDK changes: 1) explicitly mark refresh endpoints as no-retry in default Retry policy 2) when interceptor does token refresh, use a dedicated OkHttpClient with retries disabled and callTimeout smaller 3) add helper in Kotlin SDK examples to wire coroutine cancellation -> call.cancel() for service contexts
rafael: agree. also update sampleapp background-service README to show correct ordering: auth interceptor first, retry later? actually auth interceptor should be network-level so it can short-circuit before retry. we need to document recommended interceptor ordering.
infra-bot: Issue created: #7810 "Duplicate POSTs from retry+auth-refresh race in Android background service"
chloe: nina can you open a small PR that: 1) adds nonRetryClient for refresh in AuthInterceptor 2) updates sampleapp background service example 3) adds a note in onboarding about marking non-idempotent endpoints non-retriable.
nina: will do. drafting PR now and adding a tiny instrumented test that simulates connect timeout and ensures single POST.
sam: thanks — once PR lands we should roll the sampleapp patch to next alpha so QA can verify on Android 12/13 matrix.
rafael: and add a lint check in SDK that warns if a client has RetryInterceptor before AuthInterceptor. That would catch misconfigurations in sampleapps.
chloe: good idea. tagging eng-ml for perf implications of dedicated no-retry client.
nina: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1533 (draft) — will link tests and issue. thanks! :raised_hands:
